transcript.text: What makes Spanish women so attractive?
Welcome to Beauty Across Borders, episode 25, and our country for today is Spain.
The Spanish look rests on a tension: a soft, warm, feminine base with a single bolder feature laid over it.
Most of that base is skin. That warm olive undertone has a glow that softens the complexion the way good light does.
But glow and softness alone would only read as pretty. What makes Spanish women's faces memorable is the bolder feature sitting on top.
Penélope Cruz is a great example of this. She too has that warm base, but her strong dark brows and defined nose are what makes her face particularly striking.
And where that boldness comes from is partly geography. Spain is not genetically uniform.

Research suggests the makeup of someone from Barcelona in the east may differ measurably from someone in Seville to the west, a wider spread than most countries of its size, which appears to feed the range of strong features that we see across Spanish faces.
And it is this tension, that warm glow against one bolder feature, that tends to give Spanish women their characteristic beauty.
Leave a comment to let us know what country we should visit next. And if you want us to analyze your face, click the link in bio at Qoves.com.
